rationale: Sympathetic paragangliomas arise anywhere along the sympathetic chain from the skull base to the pelvis (posterior mediastinum, retroperitoneum, organ of Zuckerkandl, bladder/prostate region), spanning essentially all the connective/soft-tissue (C47) and paraganglia (C75) subsites in the ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: AJR: Extraadrenal Paragangliomas of the Body (imaging features)

site_subset_labels: Peripheral nerves/ANS of head, face and neck
rationale: Head and neck paragangliomas are, by definition, confined to the head and neck (carotid body, jugulotympanic region, vagal and laryngeal paraganglia); they do not occur across the body-wide sympathetic-chain soft-tissue sites or the heart (C380) included in the code ceiling, so they occupy only the head/neck subset.
source_name: Radiology: Imaging Cancer - Head and Neck Paragangliomas: molecular landscape

site_subset_labels: Peripheral nerves/ANS of head, face and neck
rationale: Parasympathetic paragangliomas are found almost exclusively in the head and neck / skull base along the glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves (carotid body, jugulotympanic, vagal, laryngeal), a proper subset of the code ceiling which also spans body-wide sympathetic soft-tissue sites and the heart.
source_name: PubMed 18224469 - Sporadic paraganglioma (parasympathetic tumors found almost exclusively in neck and skull base)

site_subset_labels: Peripheral nerves/ANS of head, face and neck
rationale: Synonymous with parasympathetic/head-and-neck paraganglioma; located almost exclusively in the head and neck / skull base along cranial nerves and the carotid body, a proper subset of the ceiling which also includes body-wide soft-tissue sites and the heart.
source_name: PubMed 18224469 - Sporadic paraganglioma (parasympathetic tumors found almost exclusively in neck and skull base)

rationale: Glomus jugulare tumors arise within the jugular foramen / temporal bone and extend into the middle ear; they are a fixed temporal-bone (jugulotympanic) paraganglioma restricted to the head/neck subset of the ceiling (ICD-O-3.2 maps this term to C75.5, with middle ear involvement C30.1), not to the body-wide soft-tissue/cranial-nerve sites the code allows.
source_name: StatPearls - Glomus Jugulare (arises within jugular foramen, jugular fossa of temporal bone)

rationale: Jugular paragangliomas arise from paraganglia in the adventitia of the jugular bulb within the jugular foramen (temporal bone) and involve the middle ear; a fixed temporal-bone entity restricted to the head/neck subset of the ceiling rather than the body-wide soft-tissue sites the code permits.
source_name: StatPearls - Glomus Jugulare / jugular paraganglioma (jugular foramen, temporal bone)

rationale: Tympanojugular (jugulotympanic) paragangliomas arise from paraganglia of the jugular bulb and along Jacobson/Arnold nerves in the middle ear/temporal bone; a fixed temporal-bone entity restricted to the head/neck subset of the ceiling.
source_name: BfArM ICD-O-3.2 - 8690/3 jugulotympanic/glomus jugulare/middle ear paraganglioma (C75.5)

rationale: Middle ear (glomus tympanicum) paraganglioma arises on the cochlear promontory / tympanic plexus within the middle ear and is by definition confined to the middle ear, a single-site proper subset of the code ceiling.
source_name: Current Treatment Options in Oncology - Temporal Bone Paragangliomas (glomus tympanicum limited to mesotympanum/middle ear)

rationale: Aortic body paragangliomas arise from the aortic/aortopulmonary paraganglia in the mediastinum; ICD-O-3.2 assigns this entity to C75.5 (aortic body), a single-site proper subset of the code's broad soft-tissue/cranial-nerve/paraganglia ceiling.

rationale: Aortic body tumor is a paraganglioma of the aortic/aortopulmonary paraganglia in the mediastinum; ICD-O-3.2 assigns C75.5 (aortic body), a single-site proper subset of the broad code ceiling.

rationale: Aorticopulmonary paragangliomas arise from the aortopulmonary paraganglia between the great vessels in the mediastinum; ICD-O-3.2 assigns C75.5 (aortic body/other paraganglia), a single-site proper subset of the broad code ceiling.
